p4.behavior: URL로 GraphQL 작업 또는 REST 경로 버킷을 항상 결정하는 계약은 P4가 검증한다.

about: Response classification (appendix A 1-11). responses: one GraphQL response as the tab's query snippet returns it ({status, body, headers}; headers holds only the x-rate-limit-* values), the operation it was for, and root, the dotted path where that operation's data must be (from the operation table; a [] segment is a list). outcome: ok (with the number of warnings: errors that came with data), blocked (reason challenge | account_locked: indefinite, a person clears it), rate_limited (bucket = the operation; reset = Unix seconds from the header, or null when there was none and the guard uses 900 s), login (X wants a logged-in session), csrf (X refused the ct0 token: re-read it once and retry, stop if the account changed), signature_rejected (recovery 4), contract_changed (variables no longer fit: exit 6, the skill needs an update), features_missing (names: retried once with store values, recovery 3), rotated (recovery 1-2), transient (exit 6), unavailable (exit 9), shape_changed (exit 6, the skill needs an update). Order when several apply: challenge, account_locked, rate_limited, login, csrf, signature_rejected, contract_changed, features_missing, rotated, transient, unavailable, shape_changed. signals: what the tab's hook saw in the app's own responses between or during commands, and what the guard does with it. source: code (previous transport.py), measured (planning session 2026-10-18), plan, P2 (inferred, confirmed in recon).

responses.name: challenge-html-403
responses.fact: 403 with an HTML body (a doctype, an html tag or Cloudflare's cf- markers) is a browser challenge.

responses.name: 403-json-is-not-challenge
responses.fact: A 403 with a JSON body and no lock code is not a challenge; it is a failed read.

responses.name: suspended-64
responses.fact: Error code 64 (suspended) is an account lock.

envelope.body: {"errors":[{"code":64,"message":"Your account is suspended and is not permitted to access this feature."}]}

responses.name: locked-326-with-200
responses.fact: Error code 326 (locked) is an account lock whatever the HTTP status.

envelope.body: {"errors":[{"code":326,"message":"To protect our users from spam and other malicious activity, this account is temporarily locked."}]}

responses.name: lock-outranks-rate-limit
responses.fact: A lock code in a 429 is still a lock: the person must clear it.

responses.name: rate-limit-with-reset
responses.fact: 429 is this operation's bucket running out; it resets at x-rate-limit-reset. It is not an account block.

responses.name: rate-limit-without-header
responses.fact: A 429 without the reset header resets after 900 s (the guard computes it from its clock).

responses.name: logged-out-401
responses.fact: 401 means X wants a logged-in session.

responses.name: code-32-with-200
responses.fact: Code 32 means not authenticated whatever the status.

responses.name: csrf-353
responses.fact: Code 353 is a refused CSRF token: re-read ct0 once and retry; if the logged-in account changed in between, the command stops with exit 4 (the account changed: log in to the account the command started with, or rerun).

envelope.body: {"errors":[{"code":353,"message":"This request requires a matching csrf cookie and header."}]}

responses.name: signature-rejected-404-empty
responses.fact: 404 with an empty body is X refusing the request signature (x-client-transaction-id).

responses.name: signature-rejected-whitespace
responses.fact: Whitespace only counts as empty.

responses.name: contract-422
responses.fact: 422 means the variables no longer fit the query; guessing new ones is not safe.

responses.name: contract-message
responses.fact: A validation message (must be defined, coerced Null value, GRAPHQL_VALIDATION_FAILED) is a variable contract change at any status.

envelope.body: {"errors":[{"message":"Variable \"$userId\" of required type \"NumericString!\" was not provided. must be defined","extensions":{"code":"GRAPHQL_VALIDATION_FAILED"}}]}

responses.name: features-cannot-be-null
responses.fact: 400 'features cannot be null: a, b' names feature switches the request lacked. New contract (plan recovery 3): add those names with the store's values (false when unknown) and retry once; the previous skill recorded them and failed.

envelope.body: {"errors":[{"code":336,"message":"The following features cannot be null: example_new_feature_enabled, another_flag_enabled"}]}

responses.name: errors-without-data-200
responses.fact: 200 or 404 with errors and no data suggests a rotated query id.

responses.name: errors-without-data-404
responses.fact: The same with 404 and a body.

responses.name: server-error
responses.fact: A 5xx is transient.

responses.name: non-json-200
responses.fact: A 200 that is not JSON is transient.

responses.name: empty-200
responses.fact: An empty 200 is transient.

responses.name: user-empty-data
responses.fact: UserByScreenName answering data {} means no such account.

responses.name: user-unavailable
responses.fact: A user root typed UserUnavailable (suspended, deactivated) is unavailable.

responses.name: user-root-without-numeric-id
responses.fact: A user root must carry a numeric rest_id; otherwise X changed its shape.

responses.name: batch-users-one-unavailable
responses.fact: In a batch lookup an unavailable member is not a failure; it is reported as unresolved by the feature.

responses.name: missing-root
responses.fact: A 200 with data but without the operation's root is a shape change.

responses.name: instructions-not-a-list
responses.fact: Timeline instructions must be a list of objects.

responses.name: data-with-errors-is-warning
responses.fact: Errors that come with data are warnings (shown scrubbed), not a failure.

responses.name: focal-tombstone-is-not-classify
responses.fact: A thread whose focal post is a tombstone is a valid response; the thread reader (not classification) answers unavailable.

envelope.body: {"data":{"threaded_conversation_with_injections_v2":{"instructions":[{"type":"TimelineAddEntries","entries":[{"entryId":"tweet-1850000000000000009","content":{"itemContent":{"tweet_results":{"result":{"__typename":"TweetTombstone","tombstone":{"text":{"text":"This post was deleted by the post author."}}}}}}}]}]}}}

buckets.fact: A response's x-rate-limit-limit, -remaining and -reset (all integers, reset in Unix seconds) describe the bucket of the operation that was asked; a response without all three leaves the bucket as it was. The operation name is the bucket key (the previous skill keyed by query id, which changes on rotation and would lose the bucket — plan X4).

signals.source: plan (2nd review ②), P2 R6 for the unidentified case
signals.fact: The tab's hook reads the app's own /i/api/ responses (XHR and fetch) and keeps each that may matter as a signal {path, status, codes, rate (x-rate-limit-* when readable), at}; it also notes a document move to /account/access, /i/flow/login or /login. The guard turns a signal into protection state before the next request: a lock code or a challenge or a move to /account/access is an indefinite block (exit 5); a move to a login path or code 32/401 is a login stop (exit 4); a 429 or remaining 0 is that bucket's limit only, recorded and acknowledged, stopping a command only when it uses that bucket. The bucket of a GraphQL path /i/api/graphql/<id>/<Operation> is <Operation>; of a REST path it is the path without its query.
